findings.title: Silence menu item silently does nothing in the alert list view
findings.body: When GrafanaRuleListItem renders a rule from Prometheus data only, RuleActionsButtons receives promRule but no rulerRule. The Silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu is gated only by `canSilence` (it does NOT check `rulerRule`), so it is rendered. Clicking it triggers `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is conditionally rendered as `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} ... />}`. When `rule` is undefined this short-circuits to false, so the drawer never renders. The user clicks Silence in the menu, the menu closes, and nothing visible happens, with no error feedback. Either the Silence menu item must also be gated on `rulerRule` (matching Delete/Pause) or SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer must be updated to accept promRule-based data.

findings.title: Delete menu item is no longer reachable in the alert list view (feature regression)
findings.body: The Delete menu item is rendered as `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. In the alert list view, GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons, so `rulerRule` is undefined and Delete never appears, even when `canDelete` is true (which is now legitimately computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`). Previously, the list view loaded the ruler rule for each Grafana rule and Delete was reachable. After this PR a user can view a Grafana rule in the list and edit it but cannot delete it from the list at all. Either remove `rulerRule &&` from the gate (and rework the onClick to not pass rulerRule) or document/handle the regression explicitly.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem returned from .map() is missing a `key` prop
findings.body: Inside `rules.map((ruleWithOrigin) => { ... switch (origin) { ... case 'grafana': return (<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />); ... } })` the GrafanaRuleListItem element lacks a `key` prop, while the sibling cases (`DataSourceRuleLoader`, `UnknownRuleListItem`) correctly set `key={key}`. React will emit a 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warning and state preservation for the rendered list item can be incorrect if the list reorders. Restore `key={key}` on the GrafanaRuleListItem to match the other branches.

findings.title: GrafanaGroupLoader tests assert Silence menu appears but do not verify the click works in list view
findings.body: The new tests in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx assert that the Silence menu item is in the dropdown (`expect(ui.menuItems.silence().get()).toBeInTheDocument()`). They do not click Silence to verify a silence drawer actually opens. With the new render path, `rulerRule` is undefined so the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never mounts (see finding on RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 104), making the assertion misleading: the menu item is present but the feature is non-functional. Add a test that clicks Silence and verifies a drawer/silence creation flow actually opens (or assert the menu item is NOT present when rulerRule is unavailable).

findings.title: New useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities family has no dedicated unit tests
findings.body: The newly added hooks `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, and `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (lines 287-406) are only exercised indirectly through RulesTable/AlertRuleMenu tests. Behavioral differences vs the ruler versions are subtle and untested: e.g. silence ability is `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (recording rules can never be silenced), `isProvisioned` uses promRule.provenance, and `MaybeSupported` is hardcoded to AlwaysSupported (no `isRulerAvailable` flag). Without dedicated tests a regression in any of these branches (particularly the recording-rule silencing guard, which differs from the previous ruler behavior) could land unnoticed.

findings.title: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is now deprecated but still exported and called from new code
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is marked `@deprecated` in favor of `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. The new AlertRuleMenu still computes abilities using both `useRulerRuleAbilities` AND `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (an OR), and the new RuleActionsButtons.V2 follows the same pattern. There is no public hook that combines rule + groupIdentifier into a single OR of (ruler-based, prom-based) abilities for a CombinedRule. As written, every consumer has to manually call both hooks and OR the results, which is duplicated several times already (AlertRuleMenu does it 5 times). Consider exposing a combined `useAllAlertRuleAbilitiesFor(rule: CombinedRule | GrafanaPromRuleDTO, ...)` helper so the OR logic lives in one place and isn't re-implemented (and possibly desynchronized) at every callsite.

findings.title: userEvent instance is shared across all tests instead of being recreated per test
findings.body: `const user = userEvent.setup();` is created at module scope and shared by every test in the file. userEvent accumulates internal queues/state across tests; reusing the same instance across tests can lead to flakiness or interleaved events when tests run in parallel or share state. Standard practice is to call `userEvent.setup()` (or `render` returned `user`) inside each test or in `beforeEach` for a fresh setup.
